note: Refusals whose removal (ADMIT mutant) no test notices, each with a class and a reason. DEFENSE_IN_DEPTH: another tested check refuses the same input. EQUIVALENT: no input reaches the refusal. OPEN_NO_TEST: reachable and untested (none at W27). The sweep fails on any survivor that is not listed here and on any entry that no longer survives. No REFUSE mutant survives: every refusal has a positive control.

accepted_survivors.reason: The descriptor is received with MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC, so the kernel never hands over an inheritable descriptor. The check guards against a receive call that loses that flag.
SOCK_SEQPACKET sends a record completely or not at all; sendmsg cannot return a shorter count for this message.
The envelope has a fixed shape (protocol tag, operation, canonical 36-character id) and is far below MAX_WIRE; no accepted argument can make it longer.

Fires only if the number of bytes read differs from st_size while size, mtime and ctime are identical before and after the read, i.e. if the file system reports inconsistent data. A real size change is caught by the stat comparison after the read (tested).

A change that is visible in the stat before the read is still visible in the stat after the read (tested: RESOURCE_CHANGED after the read). The early check only avoids reading a source that is already known to have changed.
More than limit bytes can only be read if the file grew after admission; growth changes st_size and is refused as RESOURCE_CHANGED by the stat comparison after the read.
st_size is part of the stamp that the preceding check compares with the admitted value, and admission already refused a size above the limit; with an unchanged stamp the size cannot exceed the limit.
A credential buffer of the wrong length makes UCRED.unpack raise struct.error, which the same function turns into UNAUTHENTICATED_PEER.
Measured: SO_PEERCRED on a non-AF_UNIX socket returns pid 0, uid -1, gid -1, which the credential range check refuses with the same code (tested with impossible credentials).
The clock value is already checked to be finite and the lifetime is at most 300 s; adding 300 to the largest finite float does not overflow (measured), so the deadline is always finite.
